title: KB refresh: streaming reconnect guidance, 429 troubleshooting, and Dedicated latency spike diagnostics
author: Elliot Price
body:
Summary: Publishes and refreshes three high-volume Known Issues & Workarounds KB pages (streaming disconnects, 429 throttling/quota, Dedicated latency spikes) as part of the escalation playbook + known-issues sprint. Content is written to be Support-safe (validated mitigations only) and includes an internal diagnostics section gated behind our internal build flag.

Why: These three themes account for a disproportionate share of escalations and time-to-mitigation. Support requested copy/pasteable guidance + a consistent set of “what to ask for” log/request fields to shorten triage and reduce back-and-forth. This PR is intended to be mirrored into the internal Confluence catalog, with “safe-to-share” excerpts aligned per PM-613.

What’s included (customer-facing): 1) Streaming disconnects: recommended client reconnect pattern for SSE, suggested timeout ranges, idempotency notes, and what metadata to include when contacting Support (request_id, region, model, SDK version, timestamp window, transport). 2) 429 throttling/quota: plain-language explanation of org/project rate limits vs burst, how to confirm current limits in Console, standard exponential backoff guidance, and when to consider Dedicated capacity. 3) Dedicated latency spikes/noisy neighbor: symptom checklist, dashboards to reference by name (latency p95/p99, queue depth, GPU utilization), and safe mitigations (autoscaling knobs, routing/fallback policy, and capacity sizing guidance) without promising instantaneous fixes.

What’s included (internal-only sections): For each page, adds an “Internal triage notes” block (hidden in public build) with deeper pointers (Grafana panel links, common misconfigurations we see, and when to engage SRE vs Dedicated oncall). No customer-identifying details included.

Validation / sign-offs: - Support Engineering (Priya / Owen) verified mitigations match what we’ve used successfully in recent tickets (SUP-4921, SUP-4922, SUP-4924). - SRE reviewed Dedicated latency spike diagnostics wording to avoid over-prescribing actions that cause paging noise (per ENG-2845 goals). - PM reviewed “safe-to-share” language and removed anything that reads like an incident admission (PM-613).

Notes: - Avoids speculative causes (e.g., “provider networking”) unless paired with a concrete observable and next action. - Keeps metrics names generic where we’re not ready to publish exact internal dashboard URLs in public docs. - Adds a consistent “What Support will ask for” section to align with the escalation required fields checklist work.

Screenshots: N/A (markdown-only).

Rollout: Merge to main, then publish in the next docs deploy window. After publish, Support will link these from the internal known-issues index + macros library.

timeline: 2026-02-18 Opened by Elliot Price. 2026-02-20 Link-check failed due to a stale anchor in the Dedicated KB page; fixed and pushed. 2026-02-21 Support review requested wording changes around retries/timeouts to avoid implying guaranteed success; updated. 2026-02-23 PM safe-to-share review completed; removed internal dashboard deep links from public sections and moved to internal-only blocks. 2026-02-24 Approved and merged (squash).
conversation: Priya Shah (review): The streaming page is close, but please avoid prescribing “retry immediately” without a backoff. Also add an explicit note: reconnect should include last_event_id only if the client supports it; otherwise start a new stream and handle duplicates. Lastly, can we add a short ‘What to send Support’ bullet list (request_id + time window + SDK version) near the top? (SUP-4921 context)

Elliot Price (author): Good call. Updated streaming guidance to: backoff with jitter (250ms -> 2s cap), and added a short “What to send Support” section with required metadata. Added the last_event_id caveat + duplication handling note.

Owen Phillips (review): 429 page: please separate “quota reached” vs “rate limit exceeded” as distinct symptoms, even if both return 429. Customers get confused and we waste cycles. Also: do not say “increase quota” as a step; instead say “verify current limits in Console and contact Support for quota review.” (SUP-4922)

Elliot Price (author): Updated with two branches: (A) sustained 429s at steady QPS (limit) vs (B) bursty spikes (burst). Reworded to “verify limits in Console; Support can review quota changes” and removed any “just increase quota” phrasing.
Wei Chen (review): Can we add SDK-specific snippets? At least Python/TS pseudo-code for exponential backoff and streaming reconnect. Even if it’s short, it’ll reduce guesswork.
Alex Martinez (review): +1 on snippets, but keep them “pattern” level and don’t hardcode exact SDK method names that change. Suggest: show pseudo-code + link to SDK retry docs page (existing).
Elliot Price (author): Added minimal pseudo-code blocks labeled “pattern (language-agnostic)” and linked to the SDK retry guidance page. Avoided concrete method names per suggestion.

Sean Gallagher (review): Dedicated latency spike page: please soften the language around ‘noisy neighbor’ so it doesn’t read like we’re blaming another customer. Also avoid telling Support to page SRE based on latency alone; add explicit thresholds / conditions for escalation (e.g., p99 > X for Y mins + elevated 5xx or queue depth growth). This ties to paging hygiene work (ENG-2845).
Kira Thompson (review): +1, and please add a section “What we can change quickly vs what needs a sizing conversation” to set expectations. Some Dedicated customers interpret any spike as a defect.

Elliot Price (author): Updated wording to “resource contention / saturation patterns” and kept “noisy neighbor” as an internal-only term. Added escalation conditions (p99 sustained + queue depth trend + customer impact) and an expectations section: immediate mitigations vs longer-term capacity plan.
Priya Shah (review): Internal-only blocks look good, but ensure they are actually hidden in public builds. Also, please remove any internal Slack channel references (I saw one in the Dedicated page).
Elliot Price (author): Confirmed internal-only blocks use the standard include gated by INTERNAL_BUILD. Removed the stray Slack reference and replaced with “contact oncall via incident process.”
PM reviewer (comment): Safe-to-share sweep done. Please remove references that imply we ‘guarantee’ mitigation within a time window. Otherwise approved for publish (PM-613).
Elliot Price (author): Removed guarantee language and changed to “targets / typical timelines vary by tier; Support will provide updates.”
Wei Chen (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping the snippets pattern-based and not overfitting to a single SDK.
Priya Shah (approval): Approved. This is aligned with what we’ve validated in the recent escalations and includes the metadata we need for triage.
Kira Thompson (approval): Approved. Dedicated section is much clearer on what’s fast vs long-term.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Escalation conditions and paging hygiene language look good.
release_notes: Docs/KB: Updated Known Issues pages for streaming reconnects, 429 troubleshooting, and Dedicated latency spikes; adds consistent ‘what to send Support’ metadata and validated mitigations. Internal-only diagnostics sections added for Support/SRE triage (not visible in public docs).
